Container.Name: fiefdom
Container.Overview:
An isometric castle-builder in the spirit of Stronghold Crusader, played in the browser. Build a settlement in the desert, run the food, ale and weapon chains, raise a garrison and hold your ground against an enemy lord who builds his own economy under the same rules you do.
⚔ Multiplayer: two to four players on one map, allied or every lord for himself, with AI lords to fill the empty seats. Players register on your server with a name, an email and a password — nothing to configure, no mail server, no external login.
⚙ Nothing to set up: no database, no API keys. Set the port, keep the Saves path on appdata, start it, open the WebUI.
💾 Saved games, custom maps and accounts are stored on the server under /data — map it to appdata and they survive updates and are the same in every browser. (Leave it unmapped and the game falls back to per-browser storage and nobody can register.)
The simulation runs in the browser, even in a match: the container serves the files, keeps the saves and passes messages between players, so it uses almost no CPU or memory. A WebGL-capable browser is required.
Container.Description: An isometric castle-builder in the spirit of Stronghold Crusader, played in the browser, alone or against two to four friends. No database and no API keys — set a port and play. Saved games, custom maps and player accounts are stored on the server under /data, so they survive updates. Every sprite in the game is procedurally generated in Blender.
Container.Requires: Nothing. A browser with WebGL support is all that is needed on the client side. For players outside your network to join a match, the game needs to be reachable from outside — a Cloudflare Tunnel or a reverse proxy will do, as long as it passes WebSocket connections through.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port the game is reached on.

Config.Name: Saves
Config.Description: Where saved games, custom maps and player accounts are kept. Leave it on appdata: this folder holds the accounts and the key that signs their sign-ins, so losing it means everyone has to register again.
